When Journeys Go Wrong

A Most journeys are boring in the best way: you set off, you get there, and nothing happens. But sometimes things go wrong — and now and then they go very wrong.

B In April 2010 a volcano in Iceland, Eyjafjallajökull, erupted under a glacier. A huge cloud of ash was moving across Europe, and airlines were afraid that the ash could damage plane engines, so many countries closed their airspace. For about a week, about 100,000 flights were cancelled, and about ten million passengers were stuck. People were trying to get home by train, by bus and even by taxi: the British comedian John Cleese took a taxi from Oslo to Brussels — about 1,500 kilometres.

C In August 2010, on a motorway into Beijing, there was a traffic jam more than 100 kilometres long. It lasted for twelve days. Some drivers were moving only one kilometre a day, and they were sleeping in their cars and lorries. Local people were walking along the road and selling them water and noodles — at much higher prices than usual.

D In Japan, people expect trains to be on time; the first high-speed line, the Shinkansen, opened in 1964. In November 2017, a train near Tokyo left a station 20 seconds early. The company said sorry to its passengers on its website.

E At home in Uzbekistan, travel is faster than ever. The Afrosiyob high-speed train, which started in 2011, goes from Tashkent to Samarkand in about two hours.

F So next time you are waiting in a long queue, or your bus is late, remember: at least you aren't sleeping in your car on a motorway near Beijing.

Grammar · past continuous

TUSHUNTIRISH — PAST CONTINUOUS

A Shakl: was / were + -ing. It was raining. · The passengers were waiting. · I wasn't listening. · Were you sleeping?

B Davom etayotgan harakatni qisqaroq harakat (Past Simple) toʻxtatadi: I was reading my book when the flight attendant spoke to me. · While we were driving to the airport, the car broke down.

C Hikoyaning fonida: It was raining, and people were hurrying to the station. Then I saw … Bir vaqtda boʻlgan ikki uzun harakat: While I was packing, my brother was sleeping.

D Istisnolar. while + Past Continuous, lekin qisqa harakat bilan when: when the plane landed — while the plane landed emas. Holat feʼllari (know, like, want, believe) Continuous da ishlatilmaydi: I didn't know the way. Zamon hikoyani oʻzgartiradi: When we arrived, the train left (biz keldik, keyin u ketdi) ≠ When we arrived, the train was leaving (u allaqachon joʻnayotgan edi).

DIQQAT — KOʻP UCHRAYDIGAN XATOLAR

1 ✗ I was read a book when … → ✓ I was reading … — was + -ing.

2 ✗ We was waiting for the bus. → ✓ We were waiting …

3 ✗ I am walking home yesterday when … → ✓ I was walking … — hozirgi emas, oʻtgan zamon.

4 ✗ While the plane landed, I was sleeping. → ✓ When the plane landed, …

5 ✗ I wasn't knowing the way. → ✓ I didn't know the way. — holat feʼli.

THE WORST JOURNEY OF MY LIFE

Last month we went to my cousin's wedding in Nukus. We set off from home at five in the morning, but there was a traffic jam on the way to the airport. At the airport there was a long queue at check-in, and then there was a delay of two hours because something was wrong with the plane. When we finally boarded and took off, there was a lot of turbulence — my little sister cried all the way. We landed at three. My uncle gave us a lift in his old car, but it broke down after ten minutes. We took a taxi, the driver got lost, and we got to the wedding at nine — just in time for the plov. On the way home I missed my train, of course.

5

Writing · a travel blog

TUSHUNTIRISH — BOGʻLOVCHI SOʻZLAR

A and qoʻshadi: The hotel is small and clean. but qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi: The flight was long, but I slept.

B so natijani bildiradi: It was windy, so I lost my hat. because sababni bildiradi: We took a ferry because I wanted to see Asia.

C when vaqtni bildiradi: When we were crossing, the wind was strong. but va so dan oldin odatda vergul qoʻyiladi — because dan oldin emas.

D Sayohat blogi: sarlavha va sana · qisqa xatboshilar · nima qildingiz, nimani koʻrdingiz va oʻzingizni qanday his qildingiz · samimiy til · oxirida ertangi rejalar.

MODEL — A BLOG POST

Istanbul, Day 1: two continents before lunch! 12 June

1 I arrived in Istanbul last night, and it's amazing! The flight from Tashkent was long, but I slept most of the way, so I wasn't tired this morning.

2 My hotel is in the old part of the city, near the Hagia Sophia. It's small but clean, and the owner, Mehmet, made us a huge Turkish breakfast.

3 After breakfast we took a ferry across the Bosphorus because I wanted to visit Asia! The trip took about twenty minutes. When we were crossing, the wind was really strong, so I lost my hat.

4 In the evening we bought simit — bread rings with sesame — from a man in the street. They were delicious and very cheap. Tomorrow we're going to the Grand Bazaar, so I'll write again soon! Has anyone got tips for shopping there?
